canonical_question: What is the specific elemental composition of the metal elements within the L4 oxide layer, and what factors explain the low metal fraction (14.3%) relative to silicon (18.1%) and oxygen (67.6%)?

question_variants.question: What specific elemental composition constitutes 'silicon and metal elements' in the L4 layer, and why is the metal content so low (14.3%) compared to silicon (18.1%) and oxygen (67.6%)?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text states L4 consists of 'complete oxides of silicon and metal elements' and provides the oxygen content (67.6%). It does not list the specific elemental identities of the 'metal elements' (e.g., Cr, Fe, Nb, Ta, etc.) or explain the specific stoichiometry leading to the low metal percentage (14.3%) relative to silicon and oxygen, other than implying they are fully oxidized.

answers.answer: The document describes L4 as consisting of 'complete oxides of silicon and metal elements'. It reports the composition as 67.6% Oxygen, 18.1% Silicon, and 14.3% Metal elements, but does not explicitly list the specific metal elements constituting the oxide nor provide a detailed stoichiometric calculation for the low metal fraction.
answers.mechanism: complete oxidation of Si and metal elements
answers.boundary_limitation: Specific metal identity and stoichiometry not detailed in the text
evidence_spans: In this paper, the Si-20Cr-20Fe coating was prepared on MoNbTaTiW RHEA by a fused slurry method.
